lesson_title: A Bucket, a Bag, a Tarpaulin
hook_text: Everything a person needs to survive a camp fits in three objects, as long as you know the numbers.
clip_script: A bucket. Twenty litres per person per day. Three to drink, three to six to cook, six to seven to wash, because hands after the toilet are how disease travels. Make it safe: boil, or chlorine, or filter then chlorine. Store it covered. A tap within 500 metres. A bag of maize meal. Two thousand one hundred kilocalories a day each, balanced: staple, protein, fat, vegetables. Breast milk for babies, soft porridge for toddlers and grandmothers, rehydration drink for the sick, nothing a family cannot eat. Cookable in big pots with little fuel, no fridge. A tarpaulin. Three and a half square metres per person, twenty-one for a family of six. Waterproof above and below. Windproof. Up in an hour. Lasts a month. Two metres from the next one. Three objects, a dozen numbers, and the briefs for the whole term.
visual_style: Whiteboard bucket, bag and tarpaulin in a row; numbers appearing beside each; a tap with a 500 metre arc; a 4 by 5 metre rectangle with six figures.
pacing: Bucket, numbers, safety, bag, groups, mix, tarpaulin, numbers, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the water, food and shelter specifications for a camp of one hundred.
